🌎 BEYOND THE 956

John Leeson, the English actor best known as the voice of K-9, the robot dog in Doctor Who, has died at 83.

His son, Guy Ducker, announced the death on Facebook on Sunday, November 1, 2026, writing: "I regret to announce the death of my father, John Ducker, a.k.a. John Leeson, at 3:03pm today after a summer of illness. The end was peaceful." He closed the announcement with a line from Shakespeare's Hamlet: "Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." No cause of death beyond the family's account of a summer of illness has been reported.

Leeson was born John Francis Christopher Ducker on March 16, 1943, in Leicester, England, and trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art. He first voiced K-9 in 1977, in "The Invisible Enemy," alongside Tom Baker's Fourth Doctor, and the character — a metal dog companion with a clipped, courteous voice — became one of the show's most beloved figures.

He went on to voice K-9 for decades, returning for the revived series in the 2006 episode "School Reunion" and in "Journey's End," and in the spin-offs K-9 and Company, The Sarah Jane Adventures, and K9. Away from Doctor Who, he was also the original voice of Bungle the bear in the children's series Rainbow, and appeared in shows including Dad's Army and Blake's 7.

Former Doctor Who showrunner Russell T Davies paid tribute, calling Leeson "a fine, fine actor" and saying it was "impossible to imagine anyone else" in the role of K-9. Leeson is survived by his wife, Judy Griffiths, whom he married in 1969, and his son, Guy.

Rest in Peace, John Leeson.

Sources: Family announcement by Guy Ducker via Facebook; The Sun; Screen Rant; Bleeding Cool.

title: Beyond the 956: John Leeson, the voice of Doctor Who's K-9, dies at 83
